findings.detail: cross_field/LATEST remains r152 and evidence-comparator/LATEST is control15/downstream24. The prior r158 leaf was therefore not repeated.

The scientist finding is correct that May git commit dates alone do not prove public availability. However, three independently cached Hugging Face directory representations pair fixed May 4-6 commit dates with snapshot-relative labels of 10-13 days, placing those readable public-page snapshots around May 16-17, before arXiv v1 on May 20. In this tested search-cache scope, pre-arXiv public visibility of the dataset repository is supported. The later Hub activity 'publication' label therefore cannot safely be interpreted as the first-public-availability date without reconciling what that activity event means.

The current public corpus is 1,819 ScienceWorld test trajectories and exposes 30 native tasks / 11 functional groups / 6 broad domains, while the paper's online evaluation is a frozen 660-episode sample across 7 task types. Current selection filenames expose 11-bank and 9-type/9-category constructions, not a self-evident 7-type/660 identity. Without row bodies or a deterministic manifest derivation, the paper evaluation stream cannot be reconstructed from the current corpus metadata alone.

scope_guards: The cached-directory witness is bounded evidence of public readability of those directory surfaces; it is not a Hub createdAt timestamp and does not establish the exact repository creation time.
No conclusion is drawn about deliberate backdating, private/public transition mechanics, or the semantic meaning of the later author-activity publication event.
No model-repository publication chronology is upgraded in this run because the two current model pages were not independently re-fetched through a stable primary metadata surface.
Cache misses for row-level files are not artifact-nonexistence evidence.
The 1,819 public corpus and 660 paper stream remain distinct until exact row-level derivation is shown.
